edition.name: Monday edition

presentation.ear_right: Inside: Uber Eats leaves couriers with their tax, Germany and Russia meet, Danish handball women beat Norway

edition.note: Built from headlines and RSS descriptions published between 08:00 on Friday and 08:00 on Monday Copenhagen time, from 132 feeds at seventeen publishers. The feeds were not polled for this edition, so nothing published after 20:41 on Sunday was read. Danish outlets decide what is news; international titles are linked where they cover the same story. Nothing else was read.

stories.headline: Britain and Norway welcome the Greenland agreement
stories.headline_short: UK and Norway back Greenland deal
stories.deck: The deal lets the US open defence areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, and it still needs approval from Inatsisartut and the Folketing.
extended: Britain and Norway welcome the agreement between Greenland, Denmark and the US, the British prime minister's office said, according to Reuters. Andy Burnham and Jonas Gahr Støre, the British and Norwegian prime ministers, met in Liverpool on Sunday, at the Labour conference.

Denmark, Greenland and the US entered into the agreement on Tuesday 22 September. It amends and extends the 1951 defence agreement, confirms the Kingdom of Denmark's sovereignty over Greenland and recognises the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination.

The US may set up defence areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig and expand Pituffik Space Base, formerly the Thule base; other sites need Danish and Greenlandic approval. The agreement opens the way for the US Golden Dome missile defence in Greenland and restricts investment in sensitive sectors from countries outside the EU and NATO.
It has no fixed end date. After signing, it must be approved first by Inatsisartut, Greenland's parliament, and then by the Folketing.
Political forces and American money men are still trying to increase their influence in the far north, a leading US analyst tells DR.

stories.headline: Uber Eats leaves its couriers to pay their own tax
stories.deck: Wolt has been made to withhold tax from couriers' pay; an expert warns Uber's couriers of large tax bills.
standard: Uber Eats runs a model in which its couriers carry the full responsibility for their own tax, according to documents Berlingske has seen, while its competitor Wolt has been forced by the authorities to withhold tax from couriers' pay.
An expert quoted by Berlingske calls the arrangement 'bold' and warns that couriers risk large tax bills. Uber denies that anything is wrong with its tax model.
lede: Uber Eats leaves its couriers with full responsibility for their own tax, documents seen by Berlingske show, while Wolt has been forced to withhold it; Uber denies anything is wrong.

stories.headline: Germany urges Russia to drop its 'course of escalation' at the first ministers' meeting since 2022
stories.deck: Wadephul told Lavrov that attacks such as the attempt in Leipzig will not shake German support for Ukraine.
standard: Germany's foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, urged Russia to abandon its 'course of escalation' with Germany, Europe and NATO when he met Sergei Lavrov in New York, an unnamed German official told AFP on Saturday. It was the two countries' first foreign ministers' meeting since Russia began the war in Ukraine in 2022.
Wadephul made clear that incidents such as the recent attempted attack in Leipzig would not shake Germany's support for Ukraine, the official said.
Lavrov told the UN that Russia is not interested in war with Europe and that Europe is the one preparing for it. A peace researcher tells DR the meeting is 'very surprising'.
lede: Germany's foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, urged Russia to drop its 'course of escalation' when he met Sergei Lavrov in New York, the first such meeting since the war in Ukraine began.

stories.headline: Missing girls from Brønderslev found unharmed
lede: Two girls aged 12 and 14 from Brønderslev, reported missing on Saturday, were found unharmed on Sunday, police say.

stories.headline: Trump repeats his promise of 5,000 dollars to adult Americans
lede: Donald Trump again promises to pay 5,000 dollars to adult Americans if the Republicans win both chambers in the midterm elections.

stories.headline: EU gives 710 million euros to people hit by crises, most of it for Africa
lede: The EU is giving 710 million euros, about 5.3 billion kroner, to people hit by crises, natural disasters and conflicts worldwide, and most of it will go to countries in Africa.

stories.headline: US Supreme Court lets the Trump administration check voters' citizenship in a disputed database
lede: The US Supreme Court has allowed the Trump administration to use a disputed database to gather information on voters' citizenship; several critics question whether the database can be trusted.

stories.headline: TikTok to pay Alabama 100 million dollars over children's addiction
lede: TikTok has settled with Alabama in a case over children's addiction, agreeing to pay 100 million dollars and limit teenagers' use in the first such settlement with a US state.

stories.headline: Tax minister signals changes to crypto tax rules
lede: Crypto tax rules cost Anders Nielsen his house and savings several years ago; the law is unchanged and his case still open, but the tax minister now signals changes.

stories.headline: Consumer Ombudsman lacks the resources to enforce new greenwashing rules
lede: New rules on green marketing have taken effect, but after budget cuts the office lacks the strength to keep up its hard line, the Consumer Ombudsman, Torben Jensen, warns.

stories.headline: Danish defence companies hire in large numbers
lede: Danish defence companies are hiring in large numbers, growing at what Jyllands-Posten calls a rarely seen pace.

stories.headline: Seven municipalities want seabed extraction moved further away
lede: Enough seabed to fill 14 swimming pools was sucked up every day last year, and seven municipalities now want the extraction moved further away.

stories.headline: Hard-pressed Faaborg-Midtfyn spends 108,000 kroner on the mayor's office
lede: Faaborg-Midtfyn Municipality, which recently received a special state grant as one of the 22 most financially pressed municipalities, is spending 108,000 kroner furnishing the mayor's office.

stories.headline: Two of Dansk Folkeparti's three councillors in Tønder leave the party
lede: Two of Dansk Folkeparti's three municipal councillors in Tønder are leaving the party after what DR calls a mysterious case.

stories.headline: 'Unknown Wanderer' identified, and a US mass murder may be solved
lede: A man found dead in a church with a false identity and 30 keys, known as 'the Unknown Wanderer', has been identified, and one of the worst US mass murders may be solved.

stories.headline: Danish handball women beat world champions Norway 34-30
lede: Denmark's women beat world champions Norway 34-30 at handball on Sunday, led by goalkeeper Anna Kristensen and playmaker Helena Elver.
